description:
This figure is a line graph comparing the ImageNet top-1 accuracy of various self-supervised learning methods against the number of parameters. The highest performing method is BYOL (200-2x), reaching approximately 78% accuracy with 400 million parameters. The lowest performing method is MoCo, achieving around 68% accuracy with 25 million parameters. Other methods include SimCLR, CMC, CPCv2-L, MoCoV2, and InfoMin, each plotted with their respective accuracy and parameter count.

Text in figure: BYOL (200-2x), Sup. (2x), BYOL (4x), BYOL (2x), SimCLR (4x), BYOL, SimCLR (2x), InfoMin, CMC, CPCv2-L, MoCoV2, MoCo, SimCLR, Number of parameters, ImageNet top-1 accuracy (%).

caption: Figure 2: BYOL 's architecture. BYOL minimizes a similarity loss between q θ ( z θ ) and sg( z ′ ξ ) , where θ are the trained weights, ξ are an exponential moving average of θ and sg means stop-gradient. At the end of training, everything but f θ is discarded, and y θ is used as the image representation.
description:
This figure is a diagram illustrating the architecture of the Bootstrap Your Own Latent (BYOL) model. It shows the flow of data through various components of the model, including the input image, views, representations, projections, and predictions. The diagram highlights the key processes and functions within the BYOL model, such as the use of exponential moving averages and the stop-gradient function. The figure also indicates the loss function used in the model and the final output, which is the image representation.

Description: The figure contains two line plots. The first plot shows the impact of batch size on the decrease in top-1 accuracy for BYOL and SimCLR (repro). The second plot shows the impact of progressively removing transformations on the decrease in top-1 accuracy for BYOL and SimCLR (repro). In the first plot, SimCLR (repro) has the highest decrease in accuracy, followed by BYOL. In the second plot, SimCLR (repro) has the highest decrease in accuracy, followed by BYOL.

caption: Figure 4: Semi-supervised training with a fraction of ImageNet labels on a ResNet50 ( × 1 ).
description:
## Description
The figure consists of two line graphs, each showing the performance of different learning methods as a function of the percentage of training data used. The left graph (a) depicts Top-1 accuracy, while the right graph (b) shows Top-5 accuracy. In both graphs, the Supervised method starts with the lowest accuracy and increases steadily. BYOL and SimCLR (repro) show intermediate performance, with BYOL slightly ahead of SimCLR. The highest performance is consistently shown by the Supervised method.

caption: Figure 5: Semi-supervised training with a fraction of ImageNet labels on multiple ResNets architecture pretrained with BYOL . Note that large networks are facing overfitting problems.
description:
Description: The figure contains four line graphs, each representing the top-1 accuracy of different ResNet architectures (ResNet-50, ResNet-101, ResNet-152, ResNet-200) when fine-tuned with varying fractions of ImageNet labels. Each graph shows multiple series, each corresponding to a different data size (e.g., 50x4, 50x2, 101x3, 101x2). The series with the highest accuracy is ResNet-200 with 200x2 data, reaching approximately 80% accuracy at 100% data usage. The lowest accuracy is observed in ResNet-50 with 50x4 data, starting at around 60% and reaching about 75% at 100% data usage.

Text in figure: ResNet-50, ResNet-101, ResNet-152, ResNet-200, 50x4, 50x2, 101x3, 101x2, 152x3, 152x2, 200x2, 200x1, Top-1 accuracy (%), Fraction of data used for fine-tuning (%).

description:
This figure is a scatter plot comparing the ImageNet top-1 accuracy of different models. The x-axis represents the number of parameters, and the y-axis represents the ImageNet top-1 accuracy percentage. The plot includes three series: Supervised (ours), Supervised [8], and BYOL. The Supervised (ours) series has the highest accuracy, followed by Supervised [8], and BYOL has the lowest accuracy. The highest accuracy is around 82% for Supervised (ours) with 400M parameters, and the lowest is around 74% for BYOL with 25M parameters.

caption: Figure 7: Effect of normalization on the ℓ 2 norm of network outputs.
description:
This figure shows two plots comparing the effect of different normalization techniques on the ℓ2 norm of network outputs during training epochs. The first plot (a) shows the ℓ2 norm of the representation, with BatchNorm having the lowest norm, followed by LayerNorm, and None having the highest norm. The second plot (b) shows the ℓ2 norm of the projection, with BatchNorm again having the lowest norm, followed by LayerNorm, and None having the highest norm. The plots indicate that BatchNorm and LayerNorm help in maintaining lower ℓ2 norms compared to no normalization.

Text in figure: Representation ℓ2-norm, Projection ℓ2-norm, Training epochs, BatchNorm, LayerNorm, None.

caption: Figure 8: BYOL sketch summarizing the method by emphasizing the neural architecture.
description:
Description: This figure is a diagram illustrating the architecture of the BYOL method for self-supervised learning. It shows two networks: an online network and a target network. Both networks process input images through a ResNet, followed by an image embedding MLP, a projection MLP, and a prediction MLP. The online network's prediction is denoted as qθ(zθ), while the target network's prediction is denoted as zξ. The diagram also includes an exponential moving average of the target network's parameters, which is used to update the target network.
